article.title: Sobrehonorificación coreana: evitar reglas automáticas
article.part: Contraste y dominio C2 — 대조와 C2 고급 운용
article.chapter: Norma, estilo y elección avanzada C2 — 규범·문체·C2 고급 선택

claims.summary: The National Institute of Korean Language says the scope of repeated honorific marking is not clearly fixed as a rule and advises against adding -시- to every predicate merely to express greater respect; social conventions and speaker–listener relations should be considered.

In its examples with subjects meaning “the problem” and “that”, the National Institute of Korean Language says forms without -시- are more appropriate; it also notes that opinions may differ about the scope of indirect honorification.

Yang (2020) distinguishes subject, object, and listener honorification and discusses controversies over their scope, supporting analysis by target and function rather than merely counting honorific forms.

The checklist separates -시- associated with a referent from listener-directed endings and cautions against turning context-dependent guidance into a universal prohibition, following the cited official response and academic framework.

links.notes: The answer states that rules do not clearly settle every usage case, asks readers to consider convention and speaker–listener relations, and cautions against adding -시- to every predicate.
The official response addresses examples with 문제/그건 as subjects and says 없어요/안 돼요 are more appropriate; it notes differences of opinion on indirect honorification.
The abstract identifies subject, object, and listener systems and says the paper discusses issues about the scope of -시- and the hearer-rating system.
Supports context-dependent caution and the refusal to formulate a universal rule.
Provides the separate target categories reflected in the checklist.
